extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating cross-lingual speech representations covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval.
extraction.license: permissive licenses allowing use and redistribution for research purposes (specific licenses vary by dataset component)
extraction.creator: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.inLanguage: 102 languages including af, am, ar, hy, as, ast, az, be, bn, bs, bg, my, yue, ca, ceb, hr, cs, da, nl, en, et, tl, fi, fr, ff, gl, lg, ka, de, el, gu, ha, he, hi, hu, is, ig, id, ga, it, ja, jv, kea, kam, kn, kk, km, ko, ky, lo, lv, lin, lt, luo, lb, mk, ms, ml, mt, cmn, mi, mr, mn, ne, nso, nb, ny, oc, or, om, ps, fa, pl, pt, pa, ro, ru, sr, sna, sd, sk, sl, so, ckb, es, sw, sv, tg, ta, te, th, tr, uk, umb, ur, uz, vi, cy, wol, xh, yo, zu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Fleurs data was collected by recording 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets in 102 languages, with between one and three recordings per sentence. Other datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) are existing publicly available datasets incorporated into the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs is based on 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets. MLS is derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli is from European Parliament sessions. CoVoST-2 is a multilingual speech translation corpus. Minds-14 is from the e-banking domain.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs, train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences respectively. For MLS, the official 10-hour splits were used. For VoxPopuli, 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data were selected. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs, between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2.3 on average). Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between 1 and 3 recordings per sentence (2.3 on average)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset. Updates will be made on the HuggingFace platform. Additional test sets may be added in the future.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech data is not abundant for all languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: XTREME-S is intended for evaluating cross-lingual speech representations. It supports training, fine-tuning, and evaluation of multilingual speech models on tasks including speech recognition, speech translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval.

name.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S, a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages.

description.evidence: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in 'universal' speech representation learning.

inLanguage.evidence: Our 102 languages cover various language families and geographical locations, from Western Europe/Americas, Eastern Europe, Central-Asia, Middle-East, North-Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, South-East Asia to CJK languages.

isLiveDataset.evidence: Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform. We expect average results not to change significantly.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102 languages. We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average), and build new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average)... For speech recognition, we use three datasets: Fleurs, MLS and VoxPopuli, which cover more than 100 languages.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets... The Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset is a large corpus derived from read audiobooks of Librivox... VoxPopuli is a multilingual speech dataset for semi-supervised learning. It contains 400k hours of unannotated speech as well as speech transcriptions and translations... CoVoST-2 is a large-scale multilingual speech translation corpus covering translations from 21 languages into English... MINDS-14 is an intent classification task from spoken data. It covers 14 intents extracted from the e-banking domain.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We build new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively... We use the official 10-hour splits provided by [6] to evaluate few-shot learning capabilities... We use the 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task... We merge monolingual datasets into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average), and build new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Training sets have around 10 hours of supervision. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average)

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform. We expect average results not to change significantly... Additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We observe in Table 4 that results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We note that the tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated... Speech data is however not abundant for all languages, so multilinguality is important to build strong representations for those languages.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in 'universal' speech representation learning... The benchmark consists of four key task types: recognition, translation, classification and retrieval.
